title: Morning Edition
dek: Saudi air travel is disrupted by renewed missile attacks; U.S. skilled-worker immigration faces a new freeze; and the quieter pages visit a Buenos Aires neighborhood and the philosophy of trust.

lead_story.headline: Missile attacks disrupt Riyadh airport and international flights
lead_story.summary: Saudi authorities reported intercepting Houthi missiles on October 8 after earlier attacks at Riyadh and Abha airports killed three people. The Houthis claimed an airport hit; airlines and flight data independently confirm major disruption.
lead_story.why_it_matters: The Yemen–Saudi escalation now reaches civilian air travel and an already strained regional aviation corridor.

items.headline: U.S. suspends eight technology employers from a green-card sponsorship program
items.summary: New and pending PERM applications involving Microsoft, Adobe and six IT outsourcing firms were frozen on October 8. Officials alleged misuse of the system, but no court finding of fraud was established.
items.why_it_matters: PERM is a route to permanent residence, not the same thing as an H-1B visa; the freeze affects workers' long-term plans.

items.headline: The world's climate-science panel is still divided over when to publish its next assessments
items.summary: IPCC members face an October 12 meeting in Addis Ababa without agreement on a timetable. Some want reports ready for the 2028 climate stocktake; others worry that haste excludes less-resourced researchers.
items.why_it_matters: A scientific assessment must be both timely enough for negotiations and inclusive enough to command trust.

items.headline: Two drone strikes damage Yandex data centers in Russia
items.summary: Yandex reported a fire and shutdown at its Ryazan-region center on October 8, followed by damaged modules at a Kaluga facility on October 9. Some services may be disrupted; the final extent is unknown.
items.why_it_matters: The war is extending physical infrastructure risks to civilian cloud and AI computing.

items.headline: EPA announces plans to propose ending methane super-emitter monitoring
items.summary: The EPA said October 7 it would propose rescinding a system using certified third-party remote sensing to flag large oil-and-gas methane releases. The proposal is not yet final.
items.why_it_matters: It would change a route from detecting major leaks to investigating and repairing them.

items.headline: September bird report finds 45% of migratory species in decline
items.summary: BirdLife International's September 11 assessment found 45% of migratory bird species declining and one in nine threatened with extinction. Migration routes cross national borders and require coordinated protection.
items.why_it_matters: The findings remain consequential weeks later because conserving one site is rarely enough for a whole migration route.

items.headline: Boedo's neighborhood culture week opens with music, crafts and local clubs
items.summary: Buenos Aires' Boedo district opened its culture week on October 4 with six murga groups, a free street festival, artisans, music and activities for children; events continue through October 11.
items.why_it_matters: A glimpse of everyday civic culture organized by neighbors rather than national institutions.

items.headline: Institutions scale cooperation by making accountability manageable
items.summary: Julien Lie-Panis argues that institutions turn a hard task—monitoring countless strangers—into a smaller task of watching a few visible monitors. Reputation and social trust remain essential.
items.why_it_matters: It explains why a good rule can work in one community yet fail in another.

worth_your_time.headline: The scientific method's surprising classroom history
worth_your_time.summary: Henry Cowles traces the familiar inquiry checklist through John Dewey's 1910 account of everyday thinking and early child psychology, challenging the idea that inquiry belongs only to experts.
worth_your_time.why_it_matters: An evergreen history of how classroom learning helped shape our image of scientific reasoning.
